correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity gives the exact equation \(p^a+1=qR_a(p)\). Reducing \(X^a+1\) modulo the monic integer polynomial \(R_a(X)\) gives an integer remainder \(B_a\). For a solution, \(R_a(p)\) divides \(B_a(p)\). The verifier excludes positive integer roots of every nonzero remainder, bounds \(p\) from the degree gap using the coefficient \(\ell_1\)-norm, and then enumerates every prime within the resulting finite bounds. A fresh independent exact replay reproduced 34 divisibility pairs, the maximal coefficient bound \(1082\) at \(a=35\), and exactly the four prime quotients claimed; candidates.tsv supplies explicit factors for all 30 composite quotients.

The current OEIS A236474 similarly tabulates examples. Neither source states that the four displayed \(p^a q\) triples exhaust every singleton-cofactor layer through exponent 49. Resultary searches returned the audited finding as the exact hit but no distinct earlier finding that implies its finite-layer completeness.
